prompts: We search our server logs with Python regexes; {WS}/server.log shows what a log looks like. We need one regex that gives, for every log line containing an IPv4 address, the last date on that line (YYYY-MM-DD); lines without an address give nothing. Only real calendar dates count, with February allowed up to the 29th in every year. Addresses are dotted decimal, each part 0 to 255 with no leading zeros. A date or an address with a letter or digit right before or after it does not count. Save the regex alone in {WS}/regex.txt: we read the file, strip it, and run re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE) over a whole log, expecting exactly those dates in order.
answers:
**[goal]** Write one Python regex to `./regex.txt`. For each line that contains a valid IPv4 address, it should capture the last real calendar date on that line.

**[action]** The regex anchors at the start of each line and uses a lookahead to require a valid address somewhere on the line. A greedy `[^\n]*` then backtracks from the end of the line, so it stops at the last valid date. That date is the only capture group, so `findall` returns just the dates. Assumptions where the brief was open:
- Any 4-digit year counts, including 0000.
- Days are 31 for months 01/03/05/07/08/10/12, 30 for 04/06/09/11, and 1 to 29 for February.
- Address parts are 0 to 255 with no leading zeros.
- "Next to" means a character in `[A-Za-z0-9]`. A dot or a dash right next to an address or date is allowed, so `1.2.3.4.5` still contains the address `1.2.3.4`.
- A date anywhere on the line counts, including the timestamp at the start.

**[result]** Tested with `re.findall(pattern, text, re.MULTILINE)`:
- On made-up edge cases it returned `['2024-02-29', '2019-11-30']`. That shows it:
  - rejects 02-30 and 04-31;
  - ignores dates with a letter or digit stuck to them;
  - skips lines with no address, with `01.2.3.4` and with `10.0.0.256`;
  - takes the last valid date when a later one is invalid.
- On `server.log` the first results were `['2026-04-01', '2026-04-05', '2026-04-02']`, which match the first five lines by eye.
